codeReview.summary: The commit adds substantial frontend preservation tests, but two core contract behaviors are not actually exercised by assertions, so regression protection is incomplete.

issues.description: VAL-SCHED-002 persistence/round-trip is not truly tested: the test titled 'calls update notifications mutation with correct payload structure' never triggers a save and only asserts mutateAsync was NOT called; the preceding 'becomes enabled when settings change' test also never changes any field. This leaves notification-save payload and persistence behavior unpinned.

VAL-SCHED-009 push subscription lifecycle is only covered by static button state checks. The suite never clicks the enable/disable browser push buttons or asserts subscribe/unsubscribe mutation calls (the only fireEvent.click uses are Run now at lines 373 and 392), so subscribe/unsubscribe behavior can regress undetected.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Mission shared-state notes for schedules are stale after this feature: they still claim no dedicated scheduled-run tests exist.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: /home/timeng/.factory/missions/600d928c-35f7-4111-b9ce-1265dff7c386/contract-work/area-schedules.md:81 states no dedicated scheduled-run/notification spec files were found, but this feature added client/src/components/Nav/SettingsTabs/Data/__tests__/ScheduledRuns.spec.tsx and client/src/components/Nav/SettingsTabs/Data/__tests__/push-sw.spec.ts.

summary: Review failed: despite broad new test additions, key expected behaviors for notification settings persistence and browser push subscribe/unsubscribe interactions are not actually asserted, leaving contract-critical regressions unguarded.
